main_body: A steampunk factory building: a large corrugated-metal roof slab (rows ~28-90) over a brick wall with arched windows, central riveted steel double door and copper pipes (rows ~92-126). A brick chimney rises on the right.
top_band: Roof is a large sloped slab of grey-blue corrugated metal from row ~28 to ~90, with a lighter top ridge and a skylight strip at rows ~30-35. Below it is an orange eave band at row ~91, then the brick front wall. The roof reads as a surface seen from above.
evidence: In a middle column the roof reads as a lighter corrugated slope with a ridge and skylight at the top, then an orange eave line at row ~91 with a dark row beneath it, then the brick wall with inset arched windows and a recessed double door. The roof is a large visible slope, comparable to the Beodeul houses, so both the top surface and the front face are clearly drawn. The roof is tall (about 62 rows) compared with the wall, but that matches the reference houses, whose roofs also dominate the facade.

style.evidence: The corrugated roof has vertical ribs in several grey-blue tones, rust specks, and a gradient from lighter to darker toward the eave. The brick wall has varied brick tones, the windows have glass reflections and lit amber panes, and the door has rivets and panels. The outlines lean to the material (dark brown beside brick, dark slate beside metal) rather than neutral black. The roof's large areas are a little regular and less textured than the Beodeul tile scallops, and the lower part of the door and wall is somewhat simple. Still, overall richness is close to the reference and does not look like a sticker.
